title: Integrative in vitro and digital twin in silico evaluation of selected natural compounds' proapoptotic and antiproliferative effects on gynecological cancer cells.
authors: Dzik, Radoslaw; Kleczka, Anna; Bregula, Agnieszka; Chwal, Joanna; Kabala-Dzik, Agata
one_liner_zh: 该研究评估天然化合物对妇科癌细胞的凋亡与增殖抑制效应，虽含数字孪生模拟，但核心为细胞实验与信号通路检测，无蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Gynecological cancers remain a major health challenge. Natural phenolics such as caffeic acid (CA) and its derivative caffeic acid phenethyl ester (CAPE) have been investigated for anticancer potential, but their comparative effects are not fully established. This study evaluated the anticancer activity of CA and CAPE in vitro, focusing on cytotoxicity (MTT) and modulation of NF-kappaB, p53, and caspase-7 pathways in PA-1 cells, complemented by in silico digital twin simulations in HeLa cells. MATERIAL AND METHODS: PA-1 cells were treated with CA or CAPE (0-200 microM) for 24 h and 48 h. Mallory's trichrome staining assessed cell morphology. Viability was measured by MTT assay, while NF-kappaB, p53, and caspase-7 levels were quantified by ELISA (mean +/- SD). IC(5)(0) values were determined using four-parameter logistic regression. Statistical significance was analysed with Friedman ANOVA (p < 0.05). In parallel, an ODE-based digital twin model simulated dose-dependent cytotoxicity and pathway activation in HeLa cells. RESULTS: Both CA and CAPE reduced PA-1 viability in a dose- and time-dependent manner, with CAPE exerting stronger effects. CA produced prolonged NF-kappaB activation, modest p53 elevation, and moderate caspase-7 induction. CAPE caused transient NF-kappaB activation followed by suppression, robust p53 upregulation, and marked caspase-7 induction, reflecting enhanced apoptosis. Digital twin simulations reproduced these dynamics, reinforcing CAPE's stronger pro-apoptotic profile. CONCLUSIONS: CA and CAPE both show anticancer activity, with CAPE demonstrating greater efficacy. Integration of in vitro assays with digital twin simulations strengthens mechanistic interpretation and highlights CAPE as a promising anticancer candidate.
abstract_zh: 目的：妇科癌症仍然是一个重大的健康挑战。天然酚类化合物，如咖啡酸（caffeic acid, CA）及其衍生物咖啡酸苯乙酯（caffeic acid phenethyl ester, CAPE），已被研究其抗癌潜力，但它们的比较效应尚未完全确立。本研究评估了CA和CAPE在体外的抗癌活性，重点关注PA-1细胞中的细胞毒性（MTT）以及NF-kappaB、p53和caspase-7通路的调节，并通过HeLa细胞中的计算机数字孪生模拟进行补充。材料与方法：将PA-1细胞用CA或CAPE（0-200微摩尔）处理24小时和48小时。采用Mallory三色染色评估细胞形态。通过MTT法测量细胞活力，同时通过ELISA定量NF-kappaB、p53和caspase-7水平（平均值±标准差）。使用四参数逻辑回归确定IC(5)(0)值。采用Friedman方差分析（p < 0.05）分析统计显著性。与此同时，基于常微分方程的数字孪生模型模拟了HeLa细胞中的剂量依赖性细胞毒性和通路激活。结果：CA和CAPE均以剂量和时间依赖性方式降低PA-1细胞活力，其中CAPE表现出更强的效应。CA引起持续的NF-kappaB激活、适度的p53升高和中度的caspase-7诱导。CAPE导致短暂的NF-kappaB激活随后抑制、显著的p53上调和明显的caspase-7诱导，反映出增强的细胞凋亡。数字孪生模拟重现了这些动态变化，进一步证实了CAPE更强的促凋亡特性。结论：CA和CAPE均显示出抗癌活性，其中CAPE表现出更高的效力。体外实验与数字孪生模拟的整合增强了机制解释，并突显CAPE作为有前景的抗癌候选药物。
